subject: Accessing and Using R: First Steps?

messages.author: c8d66ef092f48ffe
messages.subject: Accessing and Using R: First Steps?
parts:
Hello,

I think for my research it would make sense to use R. However, I'm not sure where to start, actually. Must I purchase the book in order to find a place to download specific language research applications for R? Or do I simply download from this site: http://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/ ? 

While I'm here, I'd like to ask also whether, when attempting to do collostructional analysis, R is necessary or just recommended. For example, as someone with no script-writing background at all, could I do this with SPSS and a separate concordancer/text analysis program? Not sure if an answer is too complicated to post here or not, but just thought I'd ask. 

Thanks so much for any suggestions!
Brian

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Accessing and Using R: First Steps?
parts:
- you can download R from CRAN, as you suspected;
- specific language applications are available in some packages but it
sounds as if you need a more solid background to proceed to those so
an introductory textbook would seem like a good place to start;
- for collostructions, you can use the tools provided at
<http://tinyurl.com/collostructions> so no scripting etc is required.

STG
--
